full_details: You woke after a short sleep and stayed upstairs until the house was already at work. You read the night's sheets once at the bench, and put the stone back. On the way to church you passed the bolted school door and kept your eyes on the porch. At Holy Trinity you slept the second lesson with your eyes open, and Anne let you. Your father stayed home. Dinner was at the bakehouse. The wheat was six-and-thirty shillings the quarter, said of Thursday. Anne set the penny loaf on the scale, and it met the assize. On the way home the cousin's four bays were lying at the end of the burned row, green oak, almost yellow. Tuesday's raising stayed as first said: seven of the clock, twelve men, the ale at the cousin's charge, the twenty shillings already in the timber. In the afternoon you made three bark boats. Susanna asked why the lovers did not use the door, and you said the book does not say. The corner of pie was still in the cloth when you came home. Joan took the children. On the field path you began a tale of her stile, heard yourself, and stopped. She heard the stop. Bartholomew said the wheat was thin, and said to leave it. The carrier is the eighteenth, at a horse's pace, and you will carry the pack, the sheets, and the inkhorn. You walked the rest of the field path in that silence. At supper you told the boats twice, and you kept the walk to yourself. At dusk you looked at the sheet from the orchard door and stayed on your feet.
one_sentence: You sat the service, ate at the bakehouse, made three boats, walked to Hewlands, and looked at the night's sheet under its stone.
title: Church, the boats, and the path to Hewlands
